cards.text: I sat through the whole of it in that cold room, twenty of us and Weisskopf among them. They asked why we go on building the thing, and nobody had an answer to give them.
I came here to answer Wilson and I have nothing to say that would hold. Their doubts are mine, and I can't stand up and pretend otherwise without lying to them.

I am wary, and my hands are not steady. The cyclotron hums behind the wall the way it always does, and I'd rather listen to that than to myself.

I have said out loud what I had only thought, and it did not settle anything. A doubt carried quietly is one thing, and a doubt said in a cold room with twenty men listening is heavier.
I pull my gloves back on and look at the blackboard, still chalked with the words from the meeting. My breath shows faintly in front of it.
I am tired and wary. The cyclotron is running behind me and I feel it through the floor, steady as a pulse.
